Set theory

Words: 8k Articles: 306
Foundations of mathematics OurBigBook.com

Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory

Words: 29 Articles: 1
Set theory OurBigBook.com
Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory is the usual first-order axiomatization of sets by extensionality, empty set, pairing, union, power set, infinity, separation, replacement and foundation.

Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory with choice

Words: 6
Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory OurBigBook.com
ZFC is Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory together with the axiom of choice.

Von Neumann hierarchy (Vα​)

Words: 183 Articles: 4
Set theory OurBigBook.com
The von Neumann hierarchy is
V0​=∅,Vα+1​=P(Vα​),Vλ​=⋃β<λ​Vβ​.
(1)
Every level is transitive, the levels are increasing, and every set belongs to some level.

Countable rank-initial segment cannot model ZFC

Words: 69
Von Neumann hierarchy OurBigBook.com
If α is a countable ordinal and Vα​⊨ZFC, then α must be a limit ordinal. Choose a countable cofinal sequence (αn​) in α. The internal axiom of choice gives, for every n, a bijection between Vαn​​ and some ordinal below α; that ordinal is externally countable, so every Vαn​​ is countable. Hence Vα​=⋃n​Vαn​​ is countable. But Vα​ contains the full power set P(ω), which is uncountable by Cantor theorem, a contradiction.

Lévy reflection theorem

Words: 69 Articles: 1
Von Neumann hierarchy OurBigBook.com
For every finite collection Φ of first-order formulas, there are arbitrarily large ordinals α such that, for every φ∈Φ and all parameters in Vα​,
Vα​⊨φ⟺V⊨φ.
(2)
The reflecting ordinals for Φ form a closed unbounded class.
Ordinal described by a first-order formula
Words: 30
Lévy reflection theorem OurBigBook.com
A first-order formula φ describes an ordinal α when α is the least ordinal such that Vα​⊨φ. No strongly inaccessible cardinal can be described: if Vκ​⊨φ, the Lévy reflection theorem produces some α<κ with Vα​⊨φ.

Rank of a set

Words: 19
Von Neumann hierarchy OurBigBook.com
The rank is defined by
rank(x)=supy∈x​(rank(y)+1).
(3)
It is the least ordinal α for which x⊆Vα​.

Definable power set (D(X))

Words: 348 Articles: 9
Set theory OurBigBook.com
The definable power set D(X) consists of the subsets of X definable over the structure (X,∈) by a first-order formula with parameters from X.

Constructible hierarchy (Lα​)

Words: 322 Articles: 8
Definable power set OurBigBook.com
The constructible hierarchy is defined by
L0​=∅,Lα+1​=D(Lα​),Lλ​=⋃α<λ​Lα​
(4)
for limit ordinals λ. Its union is the constructible universe L.
Constructible universe (L)
Words: 157 Articles: 3
Constructible hierarchy OurBigBook.com
The constructible universe is the inner model L=⋃α∈Ord​Lα​ obtained by iterating the definable power set. It satisfies ZFC and the Generalized continuum hypothesis.
Constructible power set (PL(A))
Words: 32
Constructible universe OurBigBook.com
For A∈L, its constructible power set is
PL(A)={X∈L:X⊆A}=P(A)∩L.
(5)
Unlike the single-stage definable power set D(A), it includes subsets of A appearing arbitrarily late in the constructible hierarchy.
Relative constructible universe (L(A))
Words: 109 Articles: 1
Constructible universe OurBigBook.com
The relative constructible universe L(A) is obtained by running the constructible hierarchy over the transitive closure of a set A, retaining A as a predicate or initial parameter. It is the smallest corresponding inner model containing the hereditary information coded by A.
Relative constructible universe can violate the continuum hypothesis
Words: 69
Relative constructible universe OurBigBook.com
Assume a transitive model M satisfies 2ℵ0​=ℵ2​. In M, encode a bijection e:ω2​→P(ω) by one set A⊆ω2​, using a fixed pairing of ω2​×ω with ω2​. Then L(A) decodes e and contains every real of M. The two models consequently have the same ω1​, and any bijection between ω1​ and the real numbers in L(A) would also be one in M. Thus L(A)⊨¬CH.
Condensation sentence for the constructible hierarchy
Words: 48
Constructible hierarchy OurBigBook.com
A condensation sentence is a fixed first-order sentence σ such that every transitive set satisfying σ is Lλ​ for a limit ordinal λ. It combines a sufficiently strong finite fragment of set theory, the assertion that every set is constructible, and the absence of a largest ordinal.
Well-order code
Words: 21
Constructible hierarchy OurBigBook.com
A well-order code is a binary relation R⊆ω×ω for which (ω,R) is a well-order. Its representation is the unique countable ordinal isomorphic to (ω,R).
Coding level of the constructible hierarchy
Words: 33
Constructible hierarchy OurBigBook.com
A level Lλ​ is a coding level when λ is a limit ordinal, the representation of every well-order code in Lλ​ is below λ, and every ordinal below λ has a well-order code in Lλ​.
Condensation lemma for the constructible universe
Words: 38
Constructible hierarchy OurBigBook.com
If X is an elementary substructure of a sufficiently large level Lθ​, then the transitive collapse of X is a level Lβ​. In particular, a countable X collapses to a level indexed by a countable ordinal.

Forcing

Words: 911 Articles: 29
Set theory OurBigBook.com
Forcing extends a model of set theory by adjoining a filter generic for a partially ordered set of finite or otherwise controlled approximations.

Standard notation for forcing

Words: 20
Forcing OurBigBook.com
In standard forcing notation, q≤p says that q is stronger than p: the smaller condition carries more information.

Jerusalem notation for forcing

Words: 19
Forcing OurBigBook.com
In Jerusalem notation, p≤q says that q is stronger than p: the larger condition carries more information.

Compatible forcing conditions

Words: 46 Articles: 1
Forcing OurBigBook.com
Two forcing conditions are compatible when they have a common stronger extension. In standard notation this means that some r satisfies r≤p,q; in Jerusalem notation for forcing it means that some r satisfies p,q≤r.
Incompatible forcing conditions
Words: 12
Compatible forcing conditions OurBigBook.com
Two forcing conditions are incompatible when they have no common stronger extension.

Dense subset of a forcing order

Words: 45 Articles: 1
Forcing OurBigBook.com
A subset D of a forcing order P is dense when every p∈P has a stronger extension q≤p in D.
Dense below a forcing condition
Words: 21
Dense subset of a forcing order OurBigBook.com
A set D⊆P is dense below p when every q≤p has an extension r≤q belonging to D.

Generic filter

Words: 223 Articles: 6
Forcing OurBigBook.com
A filter G⊆P is generic over a model M when it meets every dense subset of P belonging to M.
Rasiowa–Sikorski lemma
Words: 46
Generic filter OurBigBook.com
If M is a countable transitive model, P∈M, and p∈P, enumerate the dense subsets of P belonging to M and recursively choose a decreasing sequence starting below p that meets each one. Its upward closure is a generic filter over M containing p.
Generic extension
Words: 154 Articles: 4
Generic filter OurBigBook.com
If G is a generic filter over a countable transitive model M, the generic extension M[G] consists of the interpretations by G of all forcing names in M.
Forcing theorem
Words: 129 Articles: 3
Generic extension OurBigBook.com
The forcing theorem identifies truth in a generic extension with the forcing relation: a formula is true in M[G] exactly when some condition in G forces it.
Semantic forcing relation (p⊩φ)
Words: 18
Forcing theorem OurBigBook.com
For a countable transitive model M, semantic forcing declares p⊩φ when every generic filter G over M containing p gives M[G]⊨φ.
Syntactic forcing relation (p⊩∗φ)
Words: 32
Forcing theorem OurBigBook.com
The syntactic forcing relation is defined recursively inside the ground model from the ranks of forcing names and the logical complexity of φ. The forcing theorem proves that it agrees with the semantic forcing relation.
Separation in a generic extension
Words: 54
Forcing theorem OurBigBook.com
Let x˙,a˙1​,…,a˙n​ be forcing names and let φ be a formula. The name
y˙​={(τ,r):∃q((τ,q)∈x˙∧r≤q∧r⊩∗φ(τ,a˙1​,…,a˙n​))}
(6)
belongs to the ground model by axiom schema of separation. The forcing theorem shows that its value in a generic extension is exactly
y˙​G={z∈x˙G:M[G]⊨φ(z,a˙1G​,…,a˙nG​)}.
(7)
Consequently every generic extension satisfies the separation schema.

Countable transitive model

Words: 31
Forcing OurBigBook.com
A countable transitive model is a countable set M such that membership on M is the actual membership relation, M is transitive, and (M,∈) satisfies the specified axioms of set theory.

Cohen forcing

Words: 29
Forcing OurBigBook.com
Cohen forcing consists of finite partial approximations to a new subset or function, ordered by reverse inclusion. Meeting the ground-model dense sets makes the union a total generic object.

Eventually different forcing

Words: 30
Forcing OurBigBook.com
An eventually different condition is a finite sequence together with finitely many ground-model functions that all newly appended coordinates must avoid. The generic union eventually differs from every ground-model function.

Fn forcing (Fn(X,Y,κ))

Words: 23
Forcing OurBigBook.com
The order Fn(X,Y,κ) consists of partial functions p:X⇀Y with ∣domp∣<κ, ordered by reverse inclusion so that larger functions are stronger conditions.

Chain condition for forcing (κ-cc)

Words: 166 Articles: 3
Forcing OurBigBook.com
A forcing order has the κ-chain condition when every antichain has cardinality below κ. It preserves cardinals and cofinalities at least κ.
Possible-values lemma for chain-condition forcing
Words: 118 Articles: 1
Chain condition for forcing OurBigBook.com
Suppose P has the κ-chain condition and f˙​ is forced to be a function from an ordinal μ to an ordinal λ. For each ξ<μ, a maximal antichain in a forcing order deciding f˙​(ξ) has size below κ. Hence the ground model has a set Bξ​⊆λ of size below κ containing every possible value of f˙​(ξ).
Cardinal preservation by chain-condition forcing
Words: 58
Possible-values lemma for chain-condition forcing OurBigBook.com
If κ is a regular cardinal and P has the κ-chain condition, then forcing with P preserves every cardinal number and cofinality at least κ. Indeed, a proposed surjection f:μ→λ with μ<λ has its range contained in ⋃ξ<μ​Bξ​ from the possible-values lemma for chain-condition forcing. The regularity of κ and infinite cardinal arithmetic make this union have cardinality below the ground-model cardinal λ, a contradiction.
Countable chain condition for forcing (ccc)
Words: 23
Chain condition for forcing OurBigBook.com
A forcing order has the countable chain condition when every antichain in a forcing order is countable. Such forcing preserves cardinals and cofinalities at least ℵ1​.

Closed forcing (κ-closed)

Words: 39
Forcing OurBigBook.com
A forcing order is κ-closed when every decreasing sequence of conditions of length below κ has a lower bound. Countably closed forcing adds no new countable sequences of ground-model elements and in particular adds no new real numbers.

Antichain in a forcing order

Words: 12
Forcing OurBigBook.com
An antichain in a forcing order is a set of pairwise incompatible forcing conditions.

Centered subset of a forcing order

Words: 42 Articles: 1
Forcing OurBigBook.com
A subset of a forcing order is centered when every finite collection of its conditions has a common stronger extension.
Sigma-centered forcing (σ-centered forcing)
Words: 22
Centered subset of a forcing order OurBigBook.com
A forcing order is sigma-centered when it is the union of countably many centered subsets. Every sigma-centered forcing has the countable chain condition for forcing.

Hechler forcing

Words: 73 Articles: 1
Forcing OurBigBook.com
A Hechler condition is a pair (s,f) consisting of a finite sequence s∈ω<ω and a function f∈ωω. An extension lengthens the stem, increases the side function, and places every new stem value above the old side function. The generic union is a dominating real.
Dominating real
Words: 29
Hechler forcing OurBigBook.com
A function d∈ωω dominates h∈ωω when d(n)>h(n) for all but finitely many n. A dominating real over a ground model dominates every such function belonging to that model.

Nice name for a real

Words: 42
Forcing OurBigBook.com
For a forcing order with the countable chain condition for forcing, a real can be represented by a nice name determined by a countable antichain in a forcing order for each natural-number coordinate. This bounds the number of reals in the extension in terms of the size of the forcing order.

Finite-condition Lévy collapse (Lv(κ))

Words: 48
Forcing OurBigBook.com
The finite-condition Lévy collapse Lv(κ) consists of finite partial functions p with domp⊆κ×ω and p(α,n)<α, ordered by reverse inclusion. The generic union gives a surjection ω→α for every infinite α<κ. If κ is regular and uncountable, the Delta-system lemma at a regular uncountable cardinal proves the κ-chain condition, so the extension makes κ=ℵ1​.

Delta-system lemma

Words: 56 Articles: 1
Set theory OurBigBook.com
Every uncountable family of finite sets has an uncountable subfamily whose distinct members have the same pairwise intersection, called the root. It is also known as the sunflower lemma.

Delta-system lemma at a regular uncountable cardinal

If the second coordinate of p restricted to the K-summand covers L, it is the required surjection. Otherwise choose l0​ that it misses. Every (k,l0​) then has its preimage in the L-summand. Except possibly for the default pair, that preimage is unique, so these preimages inject K into L.
